files.lesson.md: --- order: 17 unit: congruence node: [AC9M8SP01 n2, AC9M8SP01 n3] uses: [AC9M8SP01 n1, AC9M7SP03 n1] title: Similar shapes summary: "Similar shapes are the same shape but can be different sizes, like a photo and its enlargement. Find the scale factor, use it to work out missing sides, and learn the conditions that make two triangles similar." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "How can you find the height of a tree without climbing it? Its shadow and your own shadow make two triangles of the same shape." connection: shadow-height app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8323 url: http://127.0.0.1:8323/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: sim.yml#explain-pic, caption: "A 3, 4, 5 triangle and a copy with scale factor 2: sides 6, 8, 10, the same angles." } explainClip: query: { code: "@sim.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "A scale factor" say: "Every side is multiplied by the same number." clip: - caption: { text: "Scale factor 1: the copy is the same size. Congruent.", say: "Scale factor one. The copy is congruent." } - wait: 1200 - caption: { text: "Scale factor 2: every side doubles, every angle stays.", say: "Scale factor two. Every side doubles. The angles stay the same." } - click: Make the scale factor bigger - click: Make the scale factor bigger - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "5 × 2 = 10" } - wait: 1600 --- Two shapes are **similar** when one is an **enlargement** of the other: the same shape, maybe a different size. What changes when a shape is enlarged, and what stays the same? ## Predict: double the sides ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to what happens to the angles when sides double shows whether they confuse lengths with angles." check: type: predict q: "A triangle has sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. A copy has every side doubled. What happens to its angles?" options: ["They stay the same", "They double", "They halve"] actual: "They stay the same. Doubling every side makes a bigger triangle of exactly the same shape." ``` Picture the two triangles side by side, one twice the size of the other. ## Run: scale a triangle ```step stage: run insight: "Changing the scale factor shows every side multiplied by the same number and the shape unchanged." try: { playground: board, starter: "sim.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Make a copy with scale factor 2. Divide each copy side by its matching original side. Did the angles change, as you predicted?", when: "k = 2", explain: "6 ÷ 3, 8 ÷ 4 and 10 ÷ 5 all equal 2: the same scale factor, the same angles." } ``` Then try a scale factor less than 1. What happens to the copy? In an enlargement, every length is multiplied by the same **scale factor** $k$, and every angle stays the same. Congruent shapes are similar with $k = 1$. $$k = \frac{\text{copy length}}{\text{matching original length}}$$ Triangles are similar when any one of these holds: | Condition | What matches | |---|---| | **AA** | two angles equal (so the third is too) | | **SSS** | all three pairs of sides in the same ratio | | **SAS** | two pairs of sides in the same ratio, and the angle between them equal | Translations, reflections and rotations move a shape without changing its size, so they make **congruent** shapes. An enlargement makes a **similar** shape. ## Investigate: scale factors ```step stage: investigate insight: "Find k from a matching pair and multiply; adding a fixed amount is the slip (Mia); AA is enough because the third angle follows." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A triangle has sides 4 cm, 6 cm and 8 cm. A similar triangle's shortest side is 6 cm. How long is its longest side, in cm?" answer: 12 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["10", "That adds 2 to every side. Find the scale factor: 6 ÷ 4."] explain: "k = 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5, so the longest side is 8 × 1.5 = 12 cm." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#mia" text: "Mia enlarges a photo. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: similar-add explain: "Line 2: an enlargement multiplies. k = 7 ÷ 4 = 1.75, so the 6 cm side becomes 6 × 1.75 = 10.5 cm." - check: type: question q: "Two triangles both have angles of 40° and 75°. Are they similar?" options: ["Yes, by AA: the third angles are both 65°", "No: you need the sides", "Only if they are the same size", "You cannot tell"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Two equal angles are enough for similarity.", "That would be congruent.", "Two angles fix the third, so the shape is fixed."] explain: "180 − 40 − 75 = 65 in both, so all three angles match: the same shape (AA)." ``` ### A missing side Here is the routine. ```worked \text{original } 2, 3, 4;\ \text{copy shortest} = 5 :: Match the sides: shortest with shortest. k = 5 \div 2 = 2.5 :: Scale factor: copy ÷ original. 4 \times 2.5 = 10 :: Multiply the original side by k. 10 \text{ cm} :: Check: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5 as well. ``` ### Find the mistake Read Mia's working. Does a photo stay the same shape when you add? ### Angles only ## Modify: rectangles and shadows ```step stage: modify insight: "Rectangles can have equal angles and still not be similar; similar triangles measure a tree from shadows; all squares are similar but not all rectangles." try: { playground: board, starter: "sim.yml#rect", height: 560 } tasks: - starter: "sim.yml#rect" hint: "Multiply both the width and the height by the same number." check: { type: board, text: "Make the second rectangle similar to the 4 by 2 rectangle, but not congruent.", when: "s = 1 and c = 0", explain: "Such as 8 by 4 (scale factor 2) or 6 by 3 (1.5): both sides multiplied by the same number. To be congruent as well, both sides would have to be equal: 4 by 2." } - starter: "sim.yml#rect" check: { type: board, text: "Now make a rectangle that is not similar to it. Its angles are all 90°: why is it not similar?", when: "s = 0", explain: "The width and height have different scale factors, so the shape is stretched. Equal angles are not enough for rectangles." } - check: type: number q: "A 1.5 m post casts a 2 m shadow. At the same time, a tree casts a 12 m shadow. How tall is the tree, in metres?" answer: 9 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["11.5", "That adds 10 m. The shadow is 6 times as long, so the tree is 6 times as tall."] - ["16", "Match height with height and shadow with shadow: the scale factor is 12 ÷ 2."] explain: "The sun's rays make similar triangles: k = 12 ÷ 2 = 6, so the tree is 1.5 × 6 = 9 m." - check: type: question q: "Which is true?" options: ["All squares are similar, but not all rectangles are", "All rectangles are similar", "No two squares are similar", "All rectangles are congruent"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A 4 by 2 and a 4 by 3 rectangle are not.", "Any square is an enlargement of any other.", "Congruent needs the same size."] explain: "A square's sides are always in the ratio 1 : 1. A rectangle's width and height can be in any ratio." ``` ### Similar, not congruent ### Not similar ### The tree's shadow ### Squares and rectangles ## Practise: similar shapes ```step stage: practise insight: "Finding k, missing sides and reductions, mixed; adding instead of multiplying is the planted slip; transformations link congruence and similarity; the congruence review links the two ideas." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A triangle's sides are 5, 7 and 9 cm. A similar triangle's matching sides are 15, 21 and 27 cm. What is the scale factor?" answer: 3 tolerance: 0 explain: "15 ÷ 5 = 21 ÷ 7 = 27 ÷ 9 = 3 (SSS similarity)." - check: type: number q: "A 10 cm by 6 cm rectangle is reduced so the 10 cm side becomes 5 cm. How long is the 6 cm side now, in cm?" answer: 3 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["1", "That takes 5 away. The scale factor is 5 ÷ 10 = 0.5."] explain: "k = 0.5, so 6 × 0.5 = 3 cm. A scale factor less than 1 makes the copy smaller." smaller: check: { type: number, q: "Just the long side: what do you multiply 10 by to get 5?", answer: 0.5, tolerance: 0, explain: "10 × 0.5 = 5. Every side gets multiplied by that same number." } - check: type: question q: "A triangle is moved by a transformation, and its image is similar but not congruent. Which transformation was it?" options: ["An enlargement", "A translation", "A reflection", "A rotation"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A slide keeps the size, so the image is congruent.", "A flip keeps the size, so the image is congruent.", "A turn keeps the size, so the image is congruent."] explain: "Translations, reflections and rotations keep every length, so they give congruent shapes. Only an enlargement (k ≠ 1) changes the size." - check: type: question q: "Review: two triangles have equal angles of 50° and 60°, and the sides between those angles are both 8 cm. Are they congruent?" options: ["Yes, by ASA", "No, they are only similar", "Yes, by SSS", "You cannot tell"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A matching side makes them the same size too.", "Only one side is known.", "Two angles and the side between them are enough."] explain: "Two angles and the side between them: ASA." ``` ### Scale factor ### Smaller copies ### Transformations ### Review: congruence ## Make: find the scale factor ```step stage: make insight: "Working back from one copy side to k shows they can find a scale factor and use it." try: { playground: board, starter: "sim.yml#make", height: 600 } hint: ["Which original side matches y?", "k = the copy side ÷ the matching original side."] check: { type: board, text: "The original's sides are 6, 8 and 10 cm. In the copy, side y (matching the 8 cm side) is 12 cm. Set the scale factor.", when: "y = 12", explain: "k = 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5, so the copy's sides are 9, 12 and 15 cm." } ``` Then say what the copy's other two sides are, and how you know the angles match. ## Make: a tree height, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "The tree and its shadow, and you and yours, make similar right-angled triangles, so the heights are in the same ratio as the shadows." hint: ["Match height with height and shadow with shadow.", "Find the scale factor from the two shadows."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "You are 1.5 m tall and your shadow is 2 m long. At the same moment the gum tree's shadow is 10 m long. How tall is the tree, in metres?" steps: - ["The sun makes the same angle for both, so the two right-angled triangles are similar", "same angles, so same shape"] - ["Your shadow 2 m matches the tree's shadow 10 m, so the scale factor is $10 \\div 2 = 5$", "match shadow with shadow, then divide"] - ["Tree height $= 1.5 \\times 5 = 7.5$ m", "your height matches the tree's height: multiply by the same factor"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Which sides match in the two triangles?" options: - "Your height with the tree's height, your shadow with the tree's shadow" - "Your height with the tree's shadow" - "Your shadow with the tree's height" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That pairs a height with a shadow, so the sides do not match.", "That pairs a shadow with a height. Match like with like."] answer: "7.5" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["0.3", "That divides 1.5 by 5. The tree is taller than you, so multiply by the scale factor."] - ["13.3", "That puts the ratio upside down. The scale factor is the tree's shadow ÷ your shadow."] criteria: - "I said the triangles are similar and why (the same sun angle)." - "I matched height with height and shadow with shadow." - "I found the scale factor first, then used it on 1.5 m." explain: "Scale factor = 10 ÷ 2 = 5, so the tree is 1.5 × 5 = 7.5 m tall." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The heights and shadows are made up for the task, and it only works on level ground with the shadows measured at the same moment. Draw both triangles, label the matching sides, then type the tree's height. **Also used in** - **Plans and models.** Floor plans and scale models are similar to the real thing: every length is scaled by the same factor and the angles stay. - **Photos and screens.** Enlarging a photo keeps its shape only if both sides use the same scale factor. ```teacher summary: Students scale a triangle by a scale factor, find missing sides of similar shapes, and compare rectangles that are similar, congruent or neither (AC9M8SP01, nodes 2 and 3). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can find a scale factor from a pair of matching sides. - I can use a scale factor to find a missing side. - I can say whether two shapes are congruent, similar or neither, and why. struggle: Matching the sides. Ask students to say which side matches which (shortest with shortest) before they divide. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need congruent triangles (last lesson) and multiplying by decimals. The one idea: similar means every length times the same scale factor, with the angles unchanged. The common mistake is adding a fixed amount to every side (Mia's mistake). Similarity conditions for triangles: AA, SSS (all sides in one ratio) and SAS (two sides in one ratio, the included angle equal). Only AA is practised much here; SSS appears in Practise. The link to transformations: translations, reflections and rotations give congruent shapes; an enlargement gives a similar shape. Wider: measure something tall outside with shadows and a metre ruler. running: - "Predict: ask what doubling does to a corner's angle." - "Run: ask what each copy side ÷ original side gives." - "Investigate: ask Mia whether her photo would look stretched." - "Modify: ask why two rectangles with all 90° angles may not be similar." - "Make: ask which original side matches y." - "Paper: the shadow task is worked in books; the page marks the height (7.5 m) and which sides match. Books out, then look at the page for the scale factor from the shadows." stuck: - see: A student adds the same amount to every side. ask: Would the picture look the same shape? fix: Find k by dividing, then multiply every side by k. - see: A student divides the wrong way (original ÷ copy). ask: Is the copy bigger or smaller? Should k be more or less than 1? fix: k = copy ÷ original. - see: A student says all rectangles are similar because the angles match. ask: Is a 4 by 2 rectangle the same shape as a 4 by 3? fix: For shapes other than triangles, check the sides' ratios too. stretch: A similar triangle has scale factor 3. How many times bigger is its area? Test it with the 3, 4, 5 triangle. support: A table with original sides in one column and copy sides in the next, with a ÷ column for k. leads: > This covers AC9M8SP01 nodes 2 and 3. Where it leads: proving quadrilateral properties with congruent triangles (next lesson), congruence algorithms, and trigonometry in Year 10 (which rests on similar right-angled triangles). exit: q: A 2 m by 3 m garden bed is enlarged so the 2 m side becomes 5 m. How long is the 3 m side now? a: k = 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5, so 3 × 2.5 = 7.5 m. explain: > **Similar** shapes are the same shape, maybe a different size. Every length is multiplied by the same **scale factor** k = copy ÷ original, and the angles stay the same. Congruent is similar with k = 1. Triangles are similar by **AA**, **SSS** (sides in one ratio) or **SAS** (two sides in one ratio, the angle between them equal). For other shapes, check both the angles and the ratios of the sides. ```

# Mia's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: mia
A 4 cm by 6 cm photo is enlarged so the 4 cm side becomes 7 cm.
7 − 4 = 3, so 3 cm is added to every side.
The 6 cm side becomes 6 + 3 = 9 cm.
The enlargement is 7 cm by 9 cm.
# endregion
